title_he: הוֹי צוּר עוֹלָמִים, אֲשֶׁר הֻכֵּיתָ בַּעֲדִי
review: 1:1–2 צוּר הָעוֹלָמִים … הֻכֵּיתָ — the Arabic يَا صَخْرَةَ الدُّهُور is the Rock of Ages; the Hebrew keeps צוּר (Deut 32:4) rather than the Modern סֶלַע, and הֻכֵּיתָ is the passive of Exod 17:6 (הַכֵּה בַּצּוּר), so the rock is struck and the water follows.

1:3–4 the door is opened for 'such as I' — the Arabic يَدْخُلُهُ مِثْلِي; the Hebrew keeps the relative clause rather than 'for me', so the stanza still states the general case before the personal one.
2:1–2 the blood from the side is John 19:34, and נָזַל is the verb of Judg 5:5 / Ps 147:18 for waters running down — kept so the wound is a spring, not merely an injury.
3:1 קָנִיתָ אוֹתָנוּ — 1 Cor 6:20 (נִקְנֵיתֶם בִּמְחִיר); the glossary's קָנָה is used so purchase and redemption stay one act.
3:4 עַם סְגֻלָּה — Exod 19:5 with 1 Pet 2:9; the construct is kept whole rather than 'a special people', because the phrase is a title.
4:1–3 לְבַדְּךָ is repeated at 4:1 and 4:3, as the Arabic repeats وَحْدَكَ: the aloneness is the stanza's subject, first in bearing and then in honour.
